newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas eases on milder temps, restart.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas eases on milder temps, restart.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices softened from last week's highs Monday, pressured by milder weather and the restart of a British Columbia gas plant, industry sources said.

At Sumas, Wash., the Canada-U.S. export point, gas for Tuesday delivery mostly traded in the $2.55-2.60 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) range, which is still at least 40 cents more than November's index.
Early next-day business at AECO was reported done around $3.20 per GJ, but as supplies became more available prices dove into the $2.20s.
One reason for the softening was the return of Westcoast Energy's McMahon gas processing plant in B.C., which has a capacity of about 650 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
Milder temperatures are forecast for the northwestern U.S. and western Canada by the middle of the week. However, colder temperatures are expected to return by the weekend.

At the AECO storage hub, prices were about three cents lower. Gas for Tuesday delivery traded in the C$2.30-2.35 per gigajoule (GJ) range, sources said, with the bulk of the deals reported done at the lower end of the range.
December AECO was talked around C$2.25, down from Friday's range in the high-C$2.20s to low-C$2.30s.

At Niagara, prices slipped by about three cents to about $4.10 per mmBtu amid fairly mild temperatures. Expectations for colder weather by the middle of the week in eastern Canada should boost prices as the week progresses, traders said.
